recommendations: Run t01 to t06 in outline order, playlist numbers 48 to 53, straight after a11 (47). No split: every design fits under 570 s (about 496 to 536 s estimated).

Joins: t01 opens on a11's final frame exactly (wall clock and stopwatch, '60 s = 1 min', '60 min = 1 h', 'Applications of measurement: done', 'Next: time units', '?'); a11's provisional mark is lifted. Each later video opens on the previous video's final frame. t06 closes the strand ('Time and location: done') and hands to math-s11-n01 with a flight-route map (confirmed by n01, 24 Nov 2026). Audit N9: t06 is not the last Year 11 video in playlist order, so it closes its strand only.

Each 'Next' chip quotes the next video's on-screen heading: t01 'Time units'; t02 'Elapsed time'; t03 'Latitude and longitude'; t04 'Longitude and time'; t05 'Australian time zones'; t06 'UTC'; n01 'Networks'.

Strand colour roles (fixed t01 to t06): given times and values blue; the factor, hop, offset or difference (× 60, + 12, hops, 15°, zone gaps, UTC offsets, flight times) amber; leftovers and decimal parts teal; midnight and day changes violet; answer green; mistake red (crossed slips only). t03 and t04: latitude and parallels teal, longitude and meridians blue, the equator and prime meridian amber.

Recurring models introduced once: the time ladder (t01, a01's UnitLadder with 60); the leftover splitter (t01); the decimal-hour bar (t01; relabelled for degrees and minutes in t03); the 24-hour dial (t01); the hop line (t02); the clock odometer (t02; backwards in t04; linked in t05, t06); the coded globe (t03, spinning in t04); the gridded map (t03); the longitude ruler (t04); the zone map with month slider (t04, t05); the difference ladder (t05; hung from UTC in t06).

Memory aids introduced once: t01 'Time counts in sixties: a leftover is the next unit down.'; t02 'Count up: hop to the next o'clock, then whole hours, then the minutes left.'; t03 'Lat is flat: parallels run around, north or south of the equator. Longitude lines are long: pole to pole, east or west of Greenwich.'; t04 '15 degrees is an hour, 1 degree is 4 minutes. East is ahead: the Sun gets there first.'; t05 'West is behind. From October to April the south-east goes forward an hour; Queensland, the NT and WA stay put.'; t06 'Go through UTC: back to UTC (subtract the offset), then out (add the new offset).'

Everyday anchors (no people, hands or faces; no science contexts): a song, a podcast, a playlist and a casual shift (t01); an overnight coach, a bus, an example timetable, a shift (t02); a map app, a desk globe, an atlas map (t03); the globe and Sun, ships (t04); a football final, a cricket match, a live stream, a video call, domestic flights (t05); a call to London, a Tokyo broadcast, Los Angeles, flights to Dubai and from Singapore (t06).
Prices: only the example pay rate $28.40 an hour (the site's Q4 rate, labelled 'example rate') in t01 and t02.

Facts Codex confirms in the error check: every city coordinate in t03; rounded longitudes in t04; Australian zones and daylight-saving dates and states (t05); UTC offsets and the British Summer Time and US daylight-saving dates (t06); flight times labelled 'example' (Perth to Sydney 4 h 30 min; Sydney to Perth 5 h; Sydney to Dubai 14 h 20 min; Singapore to Sydney 7 h 45 min); '−33.86, 151.21' in Sydney and '33.86°N, 151.21°E' in the open Pacific; the voice's reading of four-digit times.
New plate: ms11-desk-globe-v1.png (t03 scenes 1 and 12; t04 scenes 1 and 2). No other plate is needed.
Header strip (owner rule of 23 Nov): the focus area only, 'TIME AND LOCATION'.
